title: ENG-10 release.py: unregistered store literals + invented deployment-evidence filenames (no owner persists a deployment record); caught late at merge-time precheck
body: Two defects found during ENG-10: (A) release.py referenced store literals not in store-registry.json (fatal store-contract), patched inline; (B) release.py reads deployment.json/deploy-state.json/deploy.json but no owner writes any deployment record, so the release deployment check can never pass. Fix via workflow + RCCA + author-time guard.

rcca.root_cause: ENG-10 core/release.py introduced data-file literals (deploy.json/deploy-state.json/deployment.json/release-evidence.jsonl) that were never registered in config/store-registry.json, and invented deployment-evidence filenames that no owner writes. It was caught only by the merge-time precheck (wired_audit store_audit), not at author time, and was patched inline on the feature branch.
five_why: 1. Why did precheck fail? wired_audit.store_audit flagged 4 unregistered data-file literals in core/release.py.
2. Why were they unregistered? release.py was written without consulting/updating config/store-registry.json.
3. Why not caught earlier? No author-time (pre-commit) store-contract check; only full precheck/CI catches it.
4. Why did release.py invent filenames? No owner/contract defining where deployment evidence is persisted; deploy_providers returns a dict but never stores it.
5. Why is that allowed? ENG-10 deployment check was coded against assumed filenames instead of an owner API/contract.
rcca.corrective: Registered only owner-written stores; core/deploy_providers now persists deployment-evidence.json and core/release.py reads it; invented filenames deleted.
rcca.preventive: Added scripts/dev/store_check.py (changed-file store-contract) wired into precheck, plus scripts/dev/install_hooks.py pre-commit installer, so a new data-file literal is caught at author time (guard).
